mutations.label: L1 latest-wins inverts: the FIRST timestamped record wins, so a later failure can never clear an earlier pass -- the exact #357 defect (r91 read green forever after its first success)
L2 equal timestamps stop updating, so two records at the same instant keep the first one seen -- order starts mattering again
L3 a blank flow name is kept, so the index grows a nameless entry
L4 an unparseable recorded_at is treated as time 0 instead of 'untimed', so a corrupt row outranks nothing and silently wins the oldest slot
